description: ModelSkill is DHI's Python package for comparing simulation outputs with observations. It matches point or moving-track measurements to model results in space and time, calculates metrics such as bias and root-mean-square error, and produces scatter plots, time-series views and reports. The README demonstrates MIKE DFSU results and DFS0 observations, while stating that other models can also be assessed. Geographic coverage, dates and resolution depend on the chosen model and monitoring records; the example Dutch-coast data do not define the package's overall coverage. Public source and installation documentation are free under MIT. The current requirements specify 64-bit Python 3.12–3.14 on Windows or Linux. A limitation is that skill statistics depend on observation quality and matching choices and do not by themselves establish model validity outside the sampled conditions. The tool directly supports calibration and validation of hydraulic simulations, including MIKE+ workflows (platform-dhi-mike-plus). Its earlier candidate rejection treated model assessment as outside scope; the present brief explicitly includes resources useful for calibrating or validating infrastructure simulations.
